newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Scottish MEPs predict devolution will bring tax rise.
newsitem.headline: Scottish MEPs predict devolution will bring tax rise.

text.p: Scottish Euro-MPs said on Tuesday a Labour-run Scottish parliament would probably raise income tax.

"Theoretically, it would be possible for a Scottish parliament to vary that tax downwards but in terms of the present climate the likelihood is that the Scottish people would demand more spending on public services," David Martin, spokesman for Scotland's six Socialist Euro-MPs, told a news conference on Wednesday.
Health, education and transport services were all likely to receive more money under a Scottish parliament with taxation powers, he continued.

Scotland's Socialist Euro-MPs launched a campaign on Wednesday for a yes vote to the referendum which the British Labour Party has promised to hold on Scottish devolution if it wins the British general election, which must be held before May 22 this year.
The two-pronged referendum will ask the Scottish people whether they want a regional parliament in Edinburgh and whether that parliament should have tax raising powers.

Martin, who is a vice-president of the European Parliament, said devolution would give Scotland the best of both worlds -- a regional identity and economic powers while remaining part of Great Britain.

Even though no one yet knows if or when the referendum will be called, the Euro-MPs want to keep the issue in the limelight and have asked their constituency offices to begin today to distribute 100,000 leaflets calling for a double yes vote.

Martin pointed to the economic success of the German Laender and the Spanish autonomous region of Catalunya as examples of federal structures with a strong and constructive role at national and European level.
Labour leader Tony Blair supported a double yes vote, he said.
